title_or_artifact: Estimation of three-dimensional ground reaction forces using low-cost smart insoles
locator: Zhang D.; Liu Y.; Exell T.; Huang Y.; Zhou D.; Guo L. Intelligent Sports and Health 1(1):40–50 (2025). DOI:10.1016/j.ish.2024.12.005; full-text PDF accessed via https://www.newswise.com/pdf_docs/174014701229478_1-s2.0-S3050544525000027-main.pdf
verified_scope: Abstract and main text read: CapSense+IMU dual-stream attention estimates 3D-GRF; synchronized force plates used as reference; reported lowest NRMSE 4.1% in the stated protocol.
limitations_or_next_action: Different sensor stack (CapSense+IMU, not Velostat); not evidence of longitudinal drift robustness or biology-vs-sensor separation.

title_or_artifact: Development of a Self-Powered Piezo-Resistive Smart Insole Equipped with Low-Power BLE Connectivity for Remote Gait Monitoring
locator: de Fazio R.; Perrone E.; Velázquez R.; De Vittorio M.; Visconti P. Sensors 21(13):4539 (2021). DOI:10.3390/s21134539; https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/21/13/4539
verified_scope: Article page read in part: a Velostat piezoresistive matrix was characterized for load/repeatability/hysteresis and its firmware used a history/time-dependent corrective term for a transient effect.
limitations_or_next_action: Not a force-plate-validated 3D-GRF study and not evidence that correction separates biological change from sensor/environment change across sessions.

title_or_artifact: Simple, Commercially Viable Insole Sensor for Simultaneous Plantar Pressure and Shear Stress Measurement Using Tilted Piezoresistive Sensors
locator: Jung S.; Van Duong Q.; Kim J.; et al. International Journal of Precision Engineering and Manufacturing 27:2969–2983 (2026). DOI:10.1007/s12541-025-01388-2; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12541-025-01388-2
verified_scope: Abstract and characterization section read: five oriented piezoresistive sensors/module infer normal and shear stress; article reports notable initial drift and stabilization behavior in a sensor under cyclic testing.
limitations_or_next_action: Different sensor/module and treadmill context; no demonstrated long-term biological-versus-sensor decomposition.

title_or_artifact: Wireless pressure insoles for measuring ground reaction forces and trajectories of the centre of pressure during functional activities
locator: Scientific Reports (2023). DOI:10.1038/s41598-023-41622-3; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-41622-3
verified_scope: Abstract and methods read: two same-day sessions, force-plate comparison and test-retest assessment; AP COP trajectories were comparable, whereas ML trajectories and vGRF differed systematically from force plates.
limitations_or_next_action: Same-day test-retest is not 30-day cross-session drift correction; pressure insole does not establish Fx/Fy validation.

title_or_artifact: Wearable-sensor based walking and non-walking measures as progression markers in early to mid-stage Parkinson’s disease
locator: npj Parkinson's Disease (2026). DOI:10.1038/s41531-026-01358-z; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41531-026-01358-z
verified_scope: Abstract and methods introduction read: longitudinal wrist wearable measures were evaluated for reliability, sensitivity to within-participant change, and comparison with non-PD participants; changes were detectable from 10 months in the stated cohort.
limitations_or_next_action: Different disease, body location, and sensor; supports feasibility principles only, not knee-OA claims or insole kinetic validity.

title_or_artifact: The individuality of plantar pressure indices enables the reduction of descriptive gait data required for diagnostic purposes
locator: Scientific Reports (2025). DOI:10.1038/s41598-025-16428-0; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-16428-0
verified_scope: Abstract and introduction read: study quantified intra- versus inter-individual plantar-pressure variation in 19 healthy young women across 200 walking trials and discusses subsequent-session changes.
limitations_or_next_action: Pressure-platform study in a narrow healthy cohort; it does not decompose sensor drift and should not be generalized to OA.

title_or_artifact: Reliable Vertical Ground Reaction Force Estimation with Smart Insole During Walking
locator: Olugbon F.; Ghoreishi N.; Huang M.-C.; Xu W.; Chen D. arXiv:2501.07748 (2025). DOI:10.48550/arXiv.2501.07748; https://arxiv.org/html/2501.07748v1
verified_scope: Preprint main text read: identifies pressure-sensor drift and poor generalization as limitations; uses IMU plus center of pressed sensors (binary pressure-switch treatment) with ANN/RF/LSTM for vGRF; reports intra-/inter-participant performance.
limitations_or_next_action: Preprint, not peer reviewed; vGRF only; read scope did not establish a multi-day/session study, a 3D-GRF/COP result, or biology-versus-sensor attribution.

title_or_artifact: Evaluation of the Foot Center of Pressure Estimation from Pressure Insoles during Sidestep Cuts, Runs and Walks
locator: Blin J.; et al. Sensors 22(15):5628 (2022). PMID:35957186. DOI:10.3390/s22155628; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/35957186/
verified_scope: Abstract read: best CoP accuracy occurred when calibration motion matched the evaluated motion; accuracy also increased with vertical force and the number of involved pressure cells.
limitations_or_next_action: Does not establish a longitudinal sensor-state model; need full-method review before specifying all confounds or generalizing to project hardware.

title_or_artifact: Center of Pressure Measurement Accuracy via Insoles with a Reduced Pressure Sensor Number during Gaits
locator: Fuchs P.X.; Chen W.-H.; Shiang T.-Y. Sensors 24(15):4918 (2024). DOI:10.3390/s24154918; PMCID:PMC11315048; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11315048/
verified_scope: Abstract and article metadata read: 12 participants, 99-sensor reference insole and simulated 3–17-sensor layouts across walking/jogging/running; concordance and RMSE vary by layout and gait.
limitations_or_next_action: Simulated reduced layouts from a Pedar-X reference; not a low-cost Velostat prototype, force-plate 3D-GRF validation, or longitudinal drift study.

title_or_artifact: Benchmarking study of the forces and centre of pressure derived from a novel smart-insole against an existing pressure measuring insole and force plate
locator: Weizman Y.; Tan A.M.; Fuss F.K. Measurement 142:48–59 (2019). DOI:10.1016/j.measurement.2019.03.023; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0263224119302325
verified_scope: Abstract/preview read: benchmarked smart insole and Pedar against Kistler force plate; states that stacking/relative position of one insole to another affected accuracy and that in-shoe systems cannot measure horizontal GRF directly.
limitations_or_next_action: 2019 study; different hardware and does not test a latent sensor-state model or longitudinal change attribution.

title_or_artifact: A Low-Cost Instrumented Shoe System for Gait Phase Detection Based on Foot Plantar Pressure Data
locator: Hu X.; Duan Q.; Tang J.; Chen G.; Zhao Z.; Sun Z.; Chen C.; Qu X. IEEE Journal of Translational Engineering in Health and Medicine 12:84–96. DOI:10.1109/JTEHM.2023.3319576; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10712682/
verified_scope: Abstract and methods/discussion read: 174-cell Velostat matrix; zero-potential crosstalk method; gait-phase detection for straight and turning walking; multiple-cell regional aggregation used because cells change at different rates.
limitations_or_next_action: Gait-phase target, not force-plate 3D-GRF/COP or longitudinal measurement-integrity validation; 174 cells exceeds current direct 16-ADC assumption.

title_or_artifact: Validity and reliability of the XSENSOR in-shoe pressure measurement system
locator: Parker D.; Andrews J.; Price C. PLOS ONE 18(1):e0277971 (2023). DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0277971; https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0277971
verified_scope: Abstract and introduction read: two-day lab loading protocols quantify pressure/contact-area validity and repeatability; notes capacitive-sensor creep under extended loading and protocol-dependent suitability.
limitations_or_next_action: Bench loading and XSENSOR hardware; not human multi-session attribution of gait versus measurement-system change.

title_or_artifact: Repeatability of Vertical Ground Reaction Force Estimation During Running on the Athletics Track on 3 Different Days
locator: Scheltinga B.L.; Buurke J.H.; Kok J.N.; Reenalda J. Journal of Applied Biomechanics 41(2):167–178 (2025). DOI:10.1123/jab.2024-0126; https://journals.humankinetics.com/view/journals/jab/41/2/article-p167.xml
verified_scope: Abstract and discussion read: IMU-derived vGRF evaluated over three outdoor running days; authors model session effects and state that placement/attachment and natural day-to-day variation complicate attribution without a gold standard.
limitations_or_next_action: IMU-only outdoor study; no force plate during field sessions and not pressure-insole sensor-state separation.

title_or_artifact: Test-retest reliability and usability evaluation of a wearable plantar pressure monitoring system for linear and curved walking
locator: Scientific Reports (2025). DOI:10.1038/s41598-025-21016-3; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-21016-3
verified_scope: Abstract read: two sessions 4–7 days apart; linear/clockwise/counterclockwise tasks; reports ICC, Bland–Altman, MDC and minimum distance required for target reliability.
limitations_or_next_action: Healthy young cohort and pressure variables; no force-plate target or causal attribution of session effects.

title_or_artifact: Prediction of Three-Directional Ground Reaction Forces during Walking Using a Shoe Sole Sensor System and Machine Learning
locator: Yamaguchi T.; Takahashi Y.; Sasaki Y. Sensors 23(21):8985 (2023). DOI:10.3390/s23218985; https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/23/21/8985
verified_scope: Abstract/introduction read: a shoe-sole system with four triaxial sensors and ML estimates three-directional GRF against force plate; authors note pressure-only insoles measure vertical force and infer horizontal components indirectly.
limitations_or_next_action: Different sensing mechanism (direct triaxial sensor), task-specific models, and no longitudinal robustness claim.

title_or_artifact: A Systematic Review of Insole Sensor Technology: Recent Studies and Future Directions
locator: Santos V.M.; Gomes B.B.; Neto M.A.; Amaro A.M. Applied Sciences 14(14):6085 (2024). DOI:10.3390/app14146085; https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/14/14/6085
verified_scope: Review discussion/conclusion read: identifies incomplete real-world and longitudinal validation, the need for calibration appropriate to application, standardized testing, and reference comparisons.
limitations_or_next_action: Review-level map, not proof that no individual primary study solves a specified mechanism.

title_or_artifact: Effect of pressure insole sampling frequency on insole-measured peak force accuracy during running
locator: Elstub L.J.; Grohowski L.M.; Wolf D.N.; Owen M.K.; Noehren B.; Zelik K.E. Journal of Biomechanics 145:111387 (2022). DOI:10.1016/j.jbiomech.2022.111387; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0021929022004286
verified_scope: Abstract and introduction read: downsampled 100-Hz Pedar data shows a sampling-rate/battery/peak-force-error trade-off; peak force error remained below 3% down to 20 Hz in the studied running conditions.
limitations_or_next_action: Post-hoc downsampling of one commercial system in running; does not validate multiplexed Velostat temporal behavior, COP, 3D-GRF, or longitudinal sensor-state attribution.
